description: A dual acid bass synthesizer: two 16-step sequencers, each driving its own 303-style voice with a ladder filter, an envelope-modulated cutoff and a slide circuit.

params.text: Chooses whether the panel edits one sequence of 16 steps per track, or the song's chain of phrases.
Changes whatever the display is showing — sequence or phrase number, track length, run mode, clock division, transpose, rotate or pulses per step; a double click returns that value to its default.
Starts and stops the sequencer.
Copies from the edit cursor — 4 steps, 8 steps or the whole track, as the switch beside it is set; in song mode it copies phrase slots instead.
Writes the clipboard in at the edit cursor; a copy taken in sequence mode will not paste in song mode, or the other way about.
Returns both tracks to the first step.
Puts the edited step's note in that octave and plays it; a tied step refuses the change and flashes a warning.
Turns the gate of the edited step on or off.
Marks the edited step to be glided into from the step before it.
Sets how long a slide takes: up to one whole step for the sequencer's CV, and up to 100ms for the two synth voices.
Ties the edit cursor to the running step so editing follows playback; while it is on, the copy, paste, length and transpose buttons are refused.
Cycles the display between length, run mode and clock division, which the encoder then changes; holding it down opens the pulses-per-step setting instead.
Cycles the display between transpose and rotate for the selected track, which the encoder then changes: ±24 semitones of transpose, ±16 places of rotation.
Sets the odds that a step marked PROB fires, one figure shared by every such step in the module.
Makes the edited step fire at random rather than every pass, at the odds set by the knob beside it.
Ties the edited step to the one before it, so the note carries through without a fresh attack.
Chooses whether CPY and PST work on 4 steps, 8 steps or the whole 16-step track.
Moves the edit cursor to that step of that track and plays it; in song mode it picks that phrase slot, and while the display reads LENGTH it sets that track's length to that step.
Chooses which track is being edited, which is the track that length, run mode, clock division, transpose and rotate apply to.
Points the keyboard at the note of the edited step, so clicking a key writes that pitch.
Points the keyboard at the gate shape of the edited step, so the twelve keys choose between twelve shapes.
Accents the edited step, which cuts its decay to 200ms, lifts the amplitude envelope and opens the filter further.
Cycles the edited step's condition through 1:1, 1:2, 1:4, 1st and !1st, which sets the passes on which it plays; the same five are on this button's own right-click menu.
Sets that voice's filter cutoff, 314Hz at the bottom of the travel to 2394Hz at the top.
Sets that voice's filter resonance; the knob is squared and scaled to 0 to 10, so the ringing arrives in the last part of the travel.
Sets how far the decay envelope opens that voice's filter above the cutoff.
Sets the decay time of that voice's filter envelope, 200ms at the bottom of the travel to 2500ms at the top.
Sets how far an accented step lifts that voice's envelope and opens its filter.
Sets the gain feeding that voice's filter, one to two times, which is what saturates the ladder.
Detunes that voice by up to ±700 cents, on a squared curve so small movements near the centre are fine.
Chooses saw or square for that voice, and writing either one overwrites the Blend slider under Expert Mode.
Sets that voice's output level; past 75% the audio is pushed into a saturation rather than getting louder.
Tunes the microtuning key last clicked, ±100 cents, and that offset is applied to every note of that pitch class.
Shifts everything the sequencer plays by one octave down, nothing, or one octave up.
Sets the reference pitch, 420Hz to 460Hz, which shifts both voices; 440Hz leaves them where the CV puts them.
Gives the edited step its own release time, taken from the knob beside it, instead of the release set under Expert Mode.
Sets the release time written into the edited step while that step has REL on, 21ms to 250ms.
Clears the selected track: every note and attribute, and its length, run mode, transpose, rotate and clock division; it does nothing in song mode.

inputs.text: A trigger returns both tracks to the first step.
One pulse advances the internal pulse count; the sequence moves on a step once the pulses-per-step figure is reached.
A trigger here starts or stops the sequencer, exactly as a press of the RUN button does.
Shifts that voice's filter cutoff by 1V per octave, applied before the envelope is added.
Modulates that voice's envelope depth, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.
Modulates that voice's decay time, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.

outputs.text: That voice's audio, clamped at ±10V; neither voice is computed while both of these jacks are unpatched.

notes: There is no clock inside the module: nothing moves until a clock is patched and RUN is on.
The wide keyboard writes the note of the edited step, or its gate shape when the GATE key mode is chosen. It is drawn as one widget, so its keys cannot be clicked for help.
The dice marked RND generates a fresh acid pattern for the selected track from the settings under Randomize Track. It is not a parameter, so it cannot be clicked for help either.
The dotted labels NOTE, GATE, TIE, REL, ACC, CON, PROB and SLIDE are clickable: a dimmed one keeps that attribute out of the pattern generator, so a regenerated track holds what you set.
The strip reading INITIALIZE under the small keyboard steps through 47 temperaments with its two arrows, and clicking one of that keyboard's keys chooses which note the CENTS knob tunes.
With TwinSlide Expander placed immediately to the right, a cable in its CV, gate, slide or fine tune input replaces the internal sequencer for that track.
menu: Generate — under Randomize Track, writes a fresh pattern into the selected track from the settings below it
Scale — under Randomize Track, chooses which of 24 scales the generated notes are drawn from, or Random for a fresh draw each time
Density — under Randomize Track, sets how many of the steps are given a note, 0% to 100%
Spread — under Randomize Track, sets how far the generated notes are spread across octaves
Accent Density — under Randomize Track, sets how often a generated step is accented
Slide Density — under Randomize Track, sets how often a generated step is marked to slide
Transpose — under Randomize Track, shifts the generated pattern by up to ±12 semitones
Seed — under Randomize Track, 0 to 999, fixes which pattern comes out; it counts up after each generation so the next one differs
Pin Seed — under Randomize Track, stops the seed counting up, so Generate returns the same pattern
Start with Note — under Randomize Track, forces the first step of the pattern to carry a note
Start with Accent — under Randomize Track, accents the first note of the pattern
Expert Mode A — six sliders for synth A: VCF Range, Decay Speed, Sustain, Release, Blend and Bass Comp; the submenu reads 303 while all but Blend are at their defaults
Expert Mode B — the same six sliders for synth B
VCF Range — under Expert Mode, shifts the span the VCF knob covers, from 314Hz-2394Hz at the top of the slider down to 100Hz-760Hz at the bottom
Decay Speed — under Expert Mode, multiplies the rate the envelope decays at: 4 times in the middle, 6 times at the bottom of the slider and 2 times at the top
Sustain — under Expert Mode, sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate is high; 0% is the 303 behaviour and the default
Release — under Expert Mode, sets how long the envelope takes to fall once the gate ends, 21ms to 500ms
Blend — under Expert Mode, crossfades that voice between saw and square; the panel switch overwrites it
Bass Comp — under Expert Mode, moves the filter's feedback highpass between 150Hz and 500Hz, which sets how much low end the resonance cancels
Default clock resolution: x1, x4, x6, x12, x24 — sets the pulses per step a new instance and an Initialize start from; the module ships at x24, which needs a 96 PPQN clock for sixteenth notes
Reset on run — resets the sequence whenever RUN is switched on
Retrigger gates on reset: No, Yes, Only when Run cable is unconnected — sets whether a reset fires the gates of the step it lands on
Hold tied notes — holds the note through a tied step rather than cutting it
Single shot song — stops at the end of the song instead of looping
Portable sequence — copies or pastes the edited sequence in Rack's shared format, so it can be moved to another maker's sequencer; it is greyed out in song mode
